claims.claim: Fixed-placement feasibility has an exact matching characterization, yielding an XP exact algorithm parameterized by the number k of bugs.
claims.evidence: For fixed labeled bugs B and hosts, let A(v) be the bugs hosted in N[v]. A legal signature for v is exactly a nonempty subset of A(v). Thus distinct legal signatures are precisely a matching saturating the vertex side in the stated bipartite graph. Conversely, a saturating matching defines legal monitoring zones M(b)={v:b is in the matched signature of v}. Enumerating all binomial(n+k−1,k) host multisets and testing this matching takes f(k)n^{k+O(1)} time, hence is XP; testing successive k gives exact optimization. The checker also found exact agreement between matching and independent injective-signature backtracking in all 2,424 tested graph/placement cases.
claims.search_method: Direct proof in both directions, followed by exhaustive comparison with an independent backtracking formulation on all simple graphs of orders one through four and host multisets of at most three bugs.

claims.claim: Regional information bound: for every X⊆V, at least ceil(log2(|X|+1)) bugs must be hosted in N[X]. Moreover, the optimum is additive over connected components.
claims.evidence: Every bug in a signature of x∈X is hosted in N[x]⊆N[X]. If h bugs are hosted in N[X], vertices of X therefore receive |X| distinct nonempty subsets of an h-element set, so |X|≤2^h−1 and h≥ceil(log2(|X|+1)). For additivity, restricting a global solution to one component preserves its nonempty, pairwise-distinct local signatures. Conversely, the union of componentwise optima is feasible: bug sets of different components are disjoint, and nonempty subsets of disjoint bug sets cannot be equal. Exhaustive checks confirmed every regional inequality in 595 feasible small placements and component additivity on all 75 simple graphs through four vertices.
claims.search_method: Quantifier-level proof from signature availability, two-direction component restriction/union proof, and exhaustive small-graph verification.

claims.claim: If every connected component C has a universal safe house, then OPT is exactly sum_C ceil(log2(|C|+1)), computable in polynomial time.
claims.evidence: Applying the regional bound to X=C gives OPT(C)≥ceil(log2(|C|+1)). If u is universal in C, placing k=ceil(log2(|C|+1)) bugs at u makes every nonempty subset of those bugs available at every vertex; since 2^k−1≥|C|, distinct subsets can be assigned to all vertices. Component additivity yields the sum. Connected components and universal vertices are detectable in polynomial time. The formula also matched brute-force optima for all 60 applicable simple graphs through four vertices.
claims.witness: For each component C, cohost ceil(log2(|C|+1)) bugs at a universal vertex and assign |C| distinct nonempty subsets as signatures.
claims.search_method: Matching lower and constructive upper bounds, component summation, and exhaustive small-graph corroboration.

claims.claim: Incidence-capacity lower bound: if rho=max_v |N[v]| and a solution has k bugs, then L(n,k)≤k rho, where L(n,k) is the minimum total cardinality of n distinct nonempty subsets of a k-element set.
claims.evidence: Double-counting bug–vertex incidences gives sum_v |S(v)|=sum_b |M(b)|. A bug hosted at z monitors only vertices in N[z], so each term |M(b)| is at most rho and the total is at most k rho. Because the n signatures are distinct nonempty subsets of the k bugs, their total size is at least L(n,k). Hence L(n,k)≤k rho. The checker confirmed the inequality in every one of its 595 feasible small placements.
claims.search_method: Exact incidence double count and exhaustive small-placement corroboration.

claims.claim: The problem is exactly solvable on interval graphs of maximum degree at most two. For every connected component C of order n, OPT(C)=floor(n/2)+1; componentwise summation gives the general answer.
claims.evidence: A connected graph of maximum degree two is a path or cycle. An interval graph has no induced cycle of length at least four: choosing a cycle interval with minimum right endpoint forces both cycle neighbors to contain that endpoint, hence they form a chord. Thus the only cyclic component is K3, whose optimum is 2. For P_n, at most k signatures are singletons, so sum_v|S(v)|≥2n−k, while each bug covers at most three path vertices, giving sum_v|S(v)|≤3k and k≥ceil(n/2). For n=2t≥4, equality k=t would force all bugs to cover complete three-vertex neighborhoods from internal hosts, all signatures to be singletons or pairs, and every bug to occur as a singleton. Cohosting is then impossible, while bugs at adjacent hosts would give the two host vertices the same two-bug code. This would require t distinct nonadjacent internal hosts, but P_{2t} has at most t−1. Hence k≥t+1; P2 is excluded directly by the information bound. Bugs on odd-indexed vertices attain the bound for odd paths; for even paths, adding a bug at the last vertex does so. Exact search rejected all 4,461 below-formula path placements through order ten and verified the constructions and OPT(K3)=2.
claims.witness: For P_{2t+1}, host bugs at vertices 1,3,…,2t+1; for P_{2t}, use 1,3,…,2t−1 and 2t. Give host vertices singleton codes and intervening vertices the corresponding adjacent-bug pairs. For K3, two cohosted bugs at any vertex provide its three nonempty signatures.
claims.search_method: Structural classification, incidence lower bound with an equality-case contradiction for even paths, explicit constructions, and exact exhaustive path checks.

claims.claim: Running the source greedy algorithm in both timeline directions and taking the better result is not exact, even on a connected symmetric instance: both runs use seven bugs while OPT=6.
claims.evidence: Using exact Fraction endpoints and the source's literal lexicographic ComputeSignatures rule, the forward processing/host positions are (1,2),(2,3),(4,6),(6,7),(9,11),(11,13),(13,13); reflection gives the same seven position pairs in the reverse direction. The displayed six-bug signatures are all nonempty, distinct, and within range. For X_L={L1,L2,L3,L4}, N[X_L] is exactly {L1,…,L6}; the reflected X_R has neighborhood exactly {R1,…,R6}. These neighborhoods are disjoint, and each four-vertex region requires at least ceil(log2(5))=3 hosted bugs, proving OPT≥6. The displayed deployment proves OPT≤6. The graph is connected and invariant under reflection. As a redundant finite check, all 8,568 host multisets of at most five bugs were rejected.
claims.witness: L1=[−2/5,0], L2=[−2/5,1], L3=[3/5,2], L4=[8/5,3], L5=[8/5,4], L6=[13/5,5], U=[7/2,23/2], and Ri is the reflection of Li under x↦15−x. Host a,b,c at L2,L3,L5 and d,e,f at R5,R3,R2. Codes for L1,…,L6 are {a},{a,b},{a,b,c},{b},{b,c},{c}; codes for R1,…,R6 are {f},{e,f},{d,e,f},{e},{d,e},{d}; U has {c,d}.
claims.search_method: Literal exact simulation of the source procedure in both directions, exact code-range validation, connectivity and symmetry checks, disjoint regional certificates, and exhaustive host-multiset search through five bugs.

target_evidence: The exact target asks for either a polynomial-time approximation ratio strictly below 2 on general interval instances or an appropriate matching inapproximability result. The draft supplies neither and explicitly says the general threshold remains unresolved. Its surviving results are nevertheless material partial progress: an XP exact formulation, general lower bounds, exact restricted classes, and a counterexample showing that the natural bidirectional-greedy modification is not exact. The final writeup does not claim that the 7/6 witness rules out a below-2 approximation. Therefore VALID_PARTIAL_PROGRESS is appropriate, and claimed_resolution="PARTIAL" is ACCURATE rather than overstated or understated.
